findings.issue: loadMoveTables has the app's most intricate logic (dedup by `method:level` key, METHOD_ORDER ranking, level-then-name default sort) and is completely untested.
findings.suggestion: Extract the row/table assembly from the API fetches into a pure function taking move details + resolved moves, and unit-test dedup, method ordering (level-up/machine/egg/tutor then alphabetical) and default ordering.

findings.issue: The sort comparator's nulls-last branch is deliberately not multiplied by the direction sign — exactly the kind of subtlety a refactor breaks, with no test to catch it.
findings.suggestion: Test ascending and descending sorts over rows containing nulls (missing power/accuracy), asserting missing values land last in both directions, plus the ascending→descending toggle.

findings.issue: Pagination (NaN/out-of-range clamping, pageCount) and queryParams default-omission (home.ts:96) are untested; a regression produces wrong page links or polluted URLs like ?page=1.
findings.suggestion: Extract currentPage/pageCount/queryParams as pure functions over (page, matches, filters) and test clamping, defaults omitted, and page > 1 kept.

findings.issue: cardsFor implements the trickiest spec rule (exclude Pokémon IDs above 10000, map deoxys-normal → deoxys species) with no test; a regression puts Mega forms in every list or links cards to /pokemon/deoxys-normal.
findings.suggestion: Give it a stubbed speciesIndex and entries including an alternate form and a duplicate, and assert exclusion, species-name mapping, dedup and dex ordering.

findings.issue: The search debounce / lastSearchSent / URL-sync effect dance is stateful and race-prone (back button vs typing) but untested.
findings.suggestion: Extract the debounce/param-building into a testable function, or cover with a component test that types, navigates back and asserts the box stays in sync.

findings.issue: byName's name validation (rejecting empty or non-[a-z0-9-] names) and the 404 → NotFoundError mapping that drives the 'Not found' page are untested.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test byName rejection cases and the get() status handling (404 vs other failures) with a stubbed fetch; verify LoadState picks the not-found branch.

findings.issue: filterSpecies tests skip generation-only filtering and the zero-match case ('No Pokémon found' path).
findings.suggestion: Add a generation-only case and an empty-result case; both are cheap and each covers a distinct branch.

findings.issue: toEvolutionNode recursion (branching chains like Eevee render nested lists) has no test, nor does loadPokemonView's stat-total/height/weight formatting.
findings.suggestion: Test toEvolutionNode with a branching chain and the stat/total computation with fixture stats.

summary: The agent wrote a small but genuinely good unit suite: ten precise, behaviour-based tests of the pure formatters and the home filter, each pinning a spec-critical edge case, with zero noise. However they cover only a slice of the risk — move-table assembly, the sort comparator, pagination and URL state, the API cache and alternate-form exclusion are all untested, so most data-layer regressions would slip through once the acceptance suite stops guarding them. Net: high-quality tests, thin coverage; overall acceptable but unremarkable.
valuableTests: humanizes API names — pins mr-mime → 'Mr Mime' and thunder-punch casing, the display-name rule every list depends on
picks the English name, falling back to the humanized API name — catches a regression that would show 'mr-mime' as an h1
uses the last English flavor text with whitespace collapsed — covers \n and \f collapse and the empty case; a regex change fails it
reads IDs from resource URLs and spots alternate forms — pins the >10000 boundary that keeps Mega forms out of every list
shows missing values as an em dash — includes orMissing(0), catching the classic falsy-value bug
searches humanized names case-insensitively — would catch filtering on raw API names or case-sensitive matching
matches a type in either slot — would catch only-slot-1 filtering
combines all filters — would catch AND-composition regressions (any filter being dropped)
lowValueTests: returns everything without filters — near-trivial baseline, though it would catch accidentally-applied default filters
